title: Smallest Add-On Down Payment by How Installments Are Paid
content:
Billing help center — **Patient Payment Plans**: the smallest add-on down payment, which depends on how the plan's most recent scheduled installment was paid.

## The rule

The add-on minimum depends on how the plan's most recent scheduled installment was paid: **5.00** when it was paid by bank transfer, **10.00** when it was paid by credit or debit card, and **25.00** when it was paid any other way or no scheduled installment has been paid.

When the add-on down payment worked out for an added invoice is lower than the add-on minimum, the add-on down payment is the add-on minimum.

## The minimum by payment method

| Method of the plan's most recent scheduled-installment payment | Add-on minimum (USD) |
|---|---|
| Bank transfer (ACH) | 5.00 |
| Credit card | 10.00 |
| Debit card | 10.00 |
| Check | 25.00 |
| HSA/FSA card | 25.00 |
| No scheduled installment paid yet | 25.00 |

"Most recent scheduled installment" means the latest payment on the plan ledger posted as a scheduled installment. Down payments, arrears payments, extra-principal payments and payoffs are not scheduled installments, so a later payment of one of those kinds does not change which method is read.

## Hypothetical cases

- The last scheduled installment was drawn by bank transfer and the add-on down payment works out at 3.40: the add-on down payment is 5.00.
- The last scheduled installment was paid with a credit card and the amount works out at 12.80: 12.80 is above 10.00, so it stands.
- The last scheduled installment was paid by check; a later extra-principal payment was made by debit card; the amount works out at 18.00: the method read is the check, so the minimum is 25.00 and the add-on down payment is 25.00.
- A newly accepted plan has no scheduled installment paid yet; the amount works out at 9.00: the add-on down payment is 25.00.
